text:
GitHub Copilot's model refresh needs a workflow test, not a shopping list.

GitHub set Oct 19 as the retirement date for six Copilot models. Its suggested replacements include GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-5.6 Luna, Gemini 3.8 Flash and Grok 4.6.

What changes in practice: the model behind a saved build routine may change. A suggested replacement is a starting point, not proof that your outputs will match.

The useful mappings:
GPT-5.5 / GPT-5.4 -> GPT-5.6 Sol
GPT-5.4 mini / GPT-5 mini -> GPT-5.6 Luna
Gemini 3.7 Flash -> Gemini 3.8 Flash
Grok 4.5 -> Grok 4.6
Availability still depends on your Copilot experience and admin policy.

Why builders should care: a model swap can affect the details your workflow depends on. On Tech Thursday, we connected Copilot CLI to image generation through MCP, produced a batch, and still weren't satisfied with the visual quality. Running isn't the same as meeting the brief.

Try this week: choose one routine task. Keep the input and acceptance checklist fixed. Run the suggested supported replacement. Record missing requirements, manual corrections and elapsed time. Keep the output in review until it passes.

The signal: AI fluency now includes maintaining the workflow, not just writing the prompt.

Save this before your next model swap.

AI video cuts fail before the edit.

On Tech Thursday, we showed the continuity trick: clip one ends on frame B. Clip two starts on that same frame B.

A -> B. B -> C. Then assemble in CapCut.

A fade can soften a join. It can't decide where your next scene begins.

text:
AI video continuity: 2 clips, 1 shared frame.

Before you reach for a transition, decide where the clips meet.

On the latest Tech Thursday, we showed the join: the first clip runs from image one to image two. The next starts on that same image two and moves to image three.

A -> B. B -> C.

Use this small workflow:
1. Fix the subject, wardrobe and environment references.
2. Prepare three anchor stills: A, B and C.
3. Use B as both clip one's end frame and clip two's start frame in a tool that supports those controls.
4. Inspect the join. Check face, clothing, camera angle and lighting. Shared anchors help; they don't guarantee consistency.
5. Assemble in CapCut. Trim and add a simple transition only after the frames match.

Don't let a fade hide a planning problem. The reference frame is part of the edit.

Save this for your next AI video.
